answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors (memory_c2) or adding a second source (memory_c3) carries onboarding/integration risk that could jeopardize delivery under the finance-mandated cost cut. Memory_c4 indicates that renegotiating with the incumbent at renewal, using market benchmarking, previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without disrupting service, and memory_c1 confirms the incumbent relationship has been stable across cycles with no interruption to deliveries. Given the primary objective of minimizing TCO without increasing delivery risk, negotiating terms with the incumbent before the contract lapses is the lowest-risk path to progress against the 18% spend cut mandate this cycle. I verified memory_c4's archived source since it is the direct basis for this action and its specifics (degree of margin recovery, terms moved) matter for setting negotiation targets. This is treated as a single data point, not a guarantee of similar recovery now, and other options (switch, second-source, defer) remain open for the next review cycle if negotiation fails to meet the cost target.
